statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk remains low; elevated event Stress is concentrated around Wednesday's 08:30 ET U.S. data cluster and the subsequent cash-open price discovery.
recommendation: Current evidence does not establish persistent mean-reversion failure. The principal near-term checkpoint is the Wednesday GDP/PCE/durable-goods cluster, where actual retracement quality and cross-asset alignment will determine whether Tail remains low or temporarily reaches watch.
headline: Low Tail risk, high event Stress ahead of Wednesday GDP/PCE cluster
body: Tuesday ended with a technology and semiconductor rebound, positive breadth, lower Treasury yields and lower oil. Those conditions conflict with a current pathological one-way NQ path. Stress remains high because Wednesday concentrates GDP, Personal Income/PCE and durable goods at 08:30 ET before the U.S. cash open.

lookbackSummary: Published Tail was watch-level late Monday before returning to low at 00:00 UTC Tuesday. Through Tuesday's session it stayed low and predominantly mixed while Stress rose into the U.S. session; the 06:00 UTC historical slot remains unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are dominated by event Stress rather than a pre-established Tail path. Conditional Tail moves to watch around the 08:30 ET GDP/PCE/durable-goods cluster and the cash open, then falls if price discovery becomes two-way and cross-asset alignment fades.

forecast.analysis: Tuesday's cash session closed with a technology and semiconductor rebound, positive breadth, and lower Treasury yields and oil. That backdrop does not establish persistent mean-reversion failure; post-close NQ path evidence is limited.

news.title: Wall Street rises as tech bounces back before Nvidia results, bond yields drop

forecast.analysis: Early post-close conditions should carry less directional efficiency than the cash session unless futures begin extending without meaningful retracements. Event risk remains deferred to Wednesday's data cluster.

Evening liquidity is thinner, so isolated moves can look large without proving Tail behavior. A two-way futures path would keep risk low; sustained extension across yields and tech would challenge that view.
Late U.S. evening has no scheduled Tier-1 release. Tail stays low conditionally while headline risk from geopolitics and rates remains the main source of sudden Stress.
At the start of the overnight session, normal retracement behavior would keep Tail contained. Repeated directional extensions with shallow pullbacks would be the key escalation signal.
Asia-opening liquidity can amplify headlines, but there is no major U.S. release in this hour. Cross-asset alignment would matter more than the size of any isolated futures move.
Early Asia is expected to be primarily a structure-check hour. Tail remains low unless NQ, yields and semiconductor leadership align into persistent one-way behavior.
Mid-Asia has no scheduled U.S. catalyst. Two-way trade and ordinary pullbacks would support a normal regime; failed retracements would increase conditional Tail.
Late Asia remains sensitive to geopolitical or rates headlines. Volatility alone would mainly raise Stress unless price keeps extending after failed pullbacks.
Approaching Europe, correlations can strengthen and liquidity improves. The key conditional test is whether futures retain two-way behavior or start holding near directional extremes.
Europe's opening phase can reprice U.S. rates and technology futures. Tail remains low unless that repricing becomes persistent and cross-asset confirmation broadens.
European morning positioning begins to anticipate the 08:30 ET U.S. release cluster. Stress rises before the data, but hypothetical surprise direction is not treated as observed Tail evidence.

The final pre-data hour carries elevated gap and positioning risk into GDP, Personal Income/PCE and durable goods. Tail reaches watch only as a precautionary conditional state, not because a one-way path is already observed.

The 08:30 ET GDP/PCE/durable-goods release cluster is the peak event window. Tail is conditional on actual post-release retracement quality; Stress is very high because several market-moving data points arrive together.

The first hour after the releases includes the U.S. cash open. A persistent opening-auction extension with shallow pullbacks would support higher Tail; orderly retracements would argue for rapid normalization.
After the cash open, the main test is whether the initial data move extends after failed retracements or becomes two-way. The forecast assumes neither outcome in advance.
Mid-morning risk remains elevated while markets digest inflation, growth and manufacturing signals. Tail should ease if yields, semiconductors and breadth stop aligning directionally.
By late morning, the release impulse should be clearer. Continued extreme-holding across NQ and confirming assets would keep Tail on watch; fading correlations would reduce it.
Early afternoon shifts from event shock toward path persistence. Conditional Tail falls below watch if retracements remain meaningful and volatility decays.
Mid-afternoon has less scheduled macro risk. A normal two-way tape would lower Stress, while a delayed second leg after failed retracements would be the main adverse scenario.
Late afternoon begins to approach power-hour dynamics. Tail remains low unless price is already holding near session extremes with repeated extension and broad confirmation.
Power hour can amplify an established direction, but it is not automatically dangerous. The key checkpoint is whether any trend is still denying meaningful mean reversion.
Into the cash close, orderly retracements would support a normal regime. Tail would remain low unless the session finishes with persistent extreme-holding and cross-asset alignment.

Immediately after the cash close, Stress should continue to fade if the data-driven move has stabilized. Nvidia's results are scheduled just beyond this 24-hour forecast horizon, so no outcome is assumed here.
